newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends down on fund selling, crop outlook.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends down on fund selling, crop outlook.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower, weakened by fund long liquidation amid improving crop prospects in the U.S., Europe and Australia.

Dealers noted estimates for the amount of freeze damage to the U.S. hard red winter wheat crop continued to be revised down, crops in Europe and Australia had received much needed rains and export demand for U.S. wheat was currently sluggish.
"It looks like the funds are getting out. There is generally no (export) business. There is just no reason to buy this stuff," one dealer said.
July wheat closed 9-1/2 cents lower at $4.22 a bushel.
Other months were down 11 to one cents.

Dealers noted reports that Sparks Companies had projected U.S. hard red winter wheat production at 966 million bushels. The total was well above USDA's estimate for last year of 762 million and also higher than most expectations.
News from the Wheat Quality Council's hard red winter wheat tour was closely monitored.
Early reports suggested the wheat crop in north central and east central Kansas had the potential to yield as much as, or possibly more than it did a year ago.
